gap: No result ChatGPT got says that Synology's own 16 GB ECC module for the DS925+ (D4ES03-16G) is listed at $1,184.99 in the US. That is more than the $889.99 NAS. ChatGPT tells the shopper to upgrade the DS925+ to 8–16 GB, so that NAS reaches 20 GB for $2,074.98. The TerraMaster F4-424 Pro ships with 32 GB for $759.99 and the UGREEN DXP4800 Plus with 8 GB for $619.99.
standout_why: I checked three pages. racksandwatts.com/guides/best-nas-for-a-homelab-2026 (cited) and esp32.co.uk/best-4-bay-nas-for-docker-plex-and-family-storage (cited) both give installed and maximum RAM for each model, but neither shows a price or a price date; both only link to Amazon. esp32 says only that a RAM upgrade is 'likely for heavier stacks' on the DS925+. Neither prices the upgrade or says what Synology's warranty rule means for buying third-party RAM. ChatGPT's answers repeat 'upgrade the stock 4 GB' without a cost. Our current page has the DS925+ at $639.99 (June 2026) and gives no RAM-upgrade cost.
decides: This rules the DS925+ out as a Nextcloud pick for anyone who needs 16 GB, which ChatGPT itself recommends. Synology says it won't give full warranty or support if you add non-Synology memory, and its own 16 GB module costs more than the NAS. The pick goes to models that ship with enough RAM. The TerraMaster F4-424 Pro has 32 GB for $759.99, and the F4-425 Pro has 16 GB for $699.99. The UGREEN DXP4800 Plus at $619.99 stays the value 4-bay pick, though I couldn't price its 16 GB upgrade. For a small 1–5 user setup, the DXP2800 has 8 GB for $389.99. The DS225+ (2 GB, 6 GB maximum) at $364.99 is the weakest for Nextcloud.
